title: Thinking about amrit
hook: taking amrit is a personal step, taken when a person feels ready
tomorrow: Simran makes a list. what exactly does amrit ask of her?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Fateh walked past the kitchen to the shoe racks: the first seva, chosen, not handed. Some choices come after that one, and they are bigger.

A sign-up sheet on a cork board, a pen on a string, three names already on it. Simran is standing in the gurdwara hallway after Sunday langar, still holding a paper plate she forgot to throw away. The flyer says an amrit sanchar, the ceremony for taking amrit, is coming at the end of the month. The second name on the sheet is Jasleen, her friend from Gurmat camp. Simran picks up the pen. Puts it down. Picks it up again. Behind her, a slow voice says: that pen isn't going anywhere, beti. It's Bebe Jaswant.
screen: `A SIGN-UP SHEET. A PEN ON A STRING.` → `JASLEEN'S NAME IS ON IT.` → `BEBE: THE PEN ISN'T GOING ANYWHERE.`

segments.voice: Here's what Simran is looking at. Taking amrit is the step by which a Sikh joins the Khalsa, the community of initiated Sikhs. Five initiated Sikhs prepare amrit, a sweetened water, and give it, and those who take it commit to keep the five Ks and a daily discipline. The Sikh code of conduct, the Rehat Maryada, says who may take it: any man or woman, of any background, who is willing to keep the vows and is old enough to understand them. Notice what it doesn't set: a deadline. No age by which you must. No list of who's late. So how does a person know? The Granth answers with a picture, not a rule. On ang 1412, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: if you long to play the game of love, come to my lane with your head on your palm. Set foot on this path, and give your head without a second thought. Read slowly, the image isn't a dare. It's what readiness looks like from the inside: the head is already in your hand before you walk in. Nobody pushes it there. That's why Bebe isn't rushing her. Jasleen's name on the sheet is Jasleen's yes. It doesn't make it Simran's time. The signal isn't the sheet filling up. It's the step starting to feel like hers.
screen: `AMRIT: THE STEP INTO THE KHALSA.` · `THE CODE: WILLING, AND OLD ENOUGH.` · `NO DEADLINE, NO LIST OF WHO'S LATE.` · `ANG 1412: THE HEAD ON YOUR PALM.` · then, large: `WHEN READY.`

segments.voice: Take a scrap of paper and write one sentence by hand: I'll know I'm ready for this when… It can be about any big step in your life, not only this one. Read it back once, put the pen down, and sit with the sentence.
Thinking about amrit. Weighing the step into the Khalsa, a step taken when a person is ready, not when the sheet fills up.
Your line: when ready. The head on the palm is never pushed there. More tomorrow.

howItsDone: Gurdwaras hold amrit sanchar ceremonies from time to time; people who wish to take amrit speak with the organizers beforehand, and the decision is their own.
